attacks.claim: The embargo badge text is hard-coded to #ffffff on a background of var(--surface), which is #ffffff in the default light theme. The badge text is invisible in the default theme, and the contrast ratio is 1:1, far below WCAG 2.1 AA's 4.5:1 minimum for text.

The embargo badge renders with no visible text in light mode, the default theme, so the badge the PR exists to add is effectively broken for most editors. The text color should come from a theme token that contrasts with the surface.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: no light-theme contrast check or screenshot; the badge's text color is not themed, only its border uses var(--warn)

attacks.claim: The unpublish control is a span with an onClick handler. It is not focusable, has no role, and cannot be activated from the keyboard, which fails WCAG 2.1.1 for keyboard-only editors.

The unpublish control's only content is an icon marked aria-hidden, with no accessible name, so screen-reader users hear nothing or an unlabeled control. This fails WCAG 4.1.2 and is a destructive action.
attacks.evidence: <TrashIcon aria-hidden="true" /> with no aria-label or visually hidden text on the wrapping span

attacks.claim: The spec asks for a one-click unpublish on each queue row, but the action only renders for status 'published'. The PR does not explain or reconcile this with the spec.

handleUnpublish awaits onUnpublish with no try/catch, no pending state, and no error feedback. A failed or slow request leaves the editor unsure whether the story came down, and repeated clicks can open multiple confirm dialogs.
The embargo time shows only a date and HH:mm with no timezone label. Editors working across zones may misread when a story lifts, which is the exact question the badge is meant to answer.
The embargoed flag is computed once per render from new Date(). A row that stays mounted will keep showing the badge after the embargo lifts until something re-renders it.
attacks.evidence: const embargoed = draft.embargoUntil !== null && new Date(draft.embargoUntil) > new Date();

attacks.claim: Unpublishing a story that already went out early has external effects: caches, syndication, and shared links are not addressed. The PR does not describe whether an audit entry is written or whether downstream consumers are notified.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: no audit logging or downstream propagation described; confirm body only says "will be removed from the site and returned to drafts"

attacks.claim: Unpublish is a production write triggered from the client, but the diff shows no server-side authorization check. Only the client confirm gates it, so the server must enforce who can unpublish.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: server endpoint and authz check for onUnpublish are not in the diff
